<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The PowerShell script failed because batch files delay variable expansion inside `if` blocks. The browser launcher script needs delayed expansion enabled.

The simplest fix is to enable delayed expansion with `setlocal EnableDelayedExpansion` and use `!REPORT_URL!` instead of `%REPORT_URL%` inside the `if` block.

A simpler alternative is to bypass the browser launcher entirely and use the Windows `start` command to open the HTML file directly. This avoids the `file://` URL complexity and the delayed expansion issue altogether.

Windows file URLs require three slashes after `file://`. The delayed expansion syntax must target the correct variable—`REPORT_PATH` rather than `CD`—to convert backslashes to forward slashes properly.

Passing the absolute file path directly to the browser launcher avoids the `file://` URL complexity entirely. The PowerShell fallback script handles plain file paths correctly, so the batch script can simply pass `!REPORT_PATH!` instead of constructing a URL.
</details></think>

Inside an `if (...)` block, `%REPORT_URL%` is expanded when the block is parsed, not when it runs — so `open-browser.bat` received an empty string and reported "No URLs provided."

**Fix applied:** use `goto` instead of setting the path inside parentheses, so the report path is set before calling `open-browser.bat`:

```bat
set "REPORT_PATH=%CD%\test-results\api-test-report.html"
call scripts\open-browser.bat "%REPORT_PATH%"
```

Please double-click **`test_api.bat`** again. All 7 tests should still pass, and the HTML report should open in your browser automatically.

The `StarletteDeprecationWarning` about `httpx` is only a warning from FastAPI's test client; it does not affect test results. I can silence or fix that separately if you want.
